quizName: DMV Practice Test #5 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When riding in a group, inexperienced riders should ride near the front because:

options.text: Experienced riders can watch them more easily.
They will get lost if they are leading.
They may slow the group down as leaders.
They will ride too fast in any other position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Experienced riders can watch them more easily.
questions.explanation: In a group, inexperienced riders should ride near the front, just behind the leader. This lets experienced riders watch them easily.

questions.question: During your pre-ride inspection, you should check all of the following, except the:
questions.correctAnswerText: Reflectors.
questions.explanation: Before riding, check your tires, oil, fluid levels, headlight, taillight, turn signals, brake light, clutch, throttle, mirrors, brakes, and horn.

questions.question: When changing lanes, riders should:

options.text: Only use their mirrors to check for other vehicles.
Turn their head to look for traffic behind them.
Brake hard to let vehicles in their blind spot pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn their head to look for traffic behind them.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like any other vehicle. Always turn your head to check for traffic before changing lanes.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Left turn
questions.explanation: When an operator extends their left arm straight out to the left, it means they plan to turn left or change lanes to the left. Hand signals can be used instead of or along with turn signals.

questions.question: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield:

options.text: Is not necessary if you have a windshield.

questions.correctAnswerText: Helps protect your whole face.
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your whole face in a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield is not a good substitute for goggles or a face shield.

questions.question: When selecting a helmet, make sure it is all of the following, except:

options.text: Designed to meet U.S. Department of Transportation standards.

questions.correctAnswerText: Attractive.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation and state standards, fits snugly all around, and has no defects like cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps.

questions.question: A motorcycle operator can slow down by:
questions.correctAnswerText: Downshifting.
questions.explanation: Motorcyclists often slow down by downshifting. Note that downshifting does not activate the brake lights.

questions.question: A driver making eye contact with you:

options.text: Does not mean that they will properly yield to you.
Guarantees that they will properly yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not mean that they will properly yield to you.
questions.explanation: Do not assume eye contact means a driver will yield to you. Drivers often look directly at a motorcycle but fail to see it.

questions.question: A properly-fitted motorcycle:

options.text: Allows the rider to touch the ground with their feet while seated.
Has a seat even with the rider's waist.
Has a seat that is 10 inches above the rider's waist.
Has a seat that is 10 inches below the rider's waist.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allows the rider to touch the ground with their feet while seated.
questions.explanation: Your motorcycle fits properly when your feet can reach the ground while you are seated. Keep your feet firmly on the footrests when riding.

questions.question: When changing lanes:

options.text: Your mirrors can adequately show you your surroundings.
Do a head check in addition to using your mirrors.
Activate your turn signal and immediately move to the right or left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do a head check in addition to using your mirrors.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like any vehicle. Always turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes, along with using your mirrors.

questions.question: During the day, your headlight should:

options.text: Switch between high beam and low beam.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be used on high beam.
questions.explanation: Using your high beam during the day helps other drivers see you. Use high beam anytime you are not riding behind or toward other vehicles.

questions.question: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects the wearer from:
questions.correctAnswerText: Insects.
questions.explanation: A face shield protects you from wind, dust, dirt, rain, insects, and small rocks thrown up by other vehicles. It also protects your face if you crash.

questions.question: To reduce your reaction time, you should:

options.text: Pull in the clutch when turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cover the clutch and brakes.
questions.explanation: In high-risk areas like intersections, shopping areas, school zones, and construction zones, keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes. This reduces the time you need to react to danger.

questions.question: You should flash your brake light when:

options.text: You will slow down where drivers do not expect it.
There is a stop sign ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will slow down where drivers do not expect it.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle brake lights are harder to see than car brake lights. Flash your brake light when slowing down in places where drivers might not expect it, such as the middle of a block or near an alley.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:
questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Rectangular signs with white background and black letters show traffic rules like speed limits. You must follow all rules posted on these signs.

questions.question: In a normal turn:

options.text: The motorcycle and rider should lean together.
The motorcycle and rider should lean in opposite directions.
The motorcycle should lean, but the rider should not.
The rider should lean, but the motorcycle should not.

questions.correctAnswerText: The motorcycle and rider should lean together.
questions.explanation: In normal turns, the motorcycle and rider lean at the same angle together. In slow, tight turns, only the motorcycle leans while the rider stays upright.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while riding and you must stop, you should:

options.text: Shift your weight toward the good tire.
Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
Use both brakes and stop quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat, grip both handle grips firmly and ease off the throttle. Keep the motorcycle straight. If you must brake, slowly apply the brake of the tire that is not flat. As you slow down, move to the side of the road, pull in the clutch, and stop.

questions.question: Making eye contact with other drivers:

options.text: Is the best way to know that they see you.
Is not worth the effort it takes.
Does not guarantee they will yield to you.
Guarantees that they will yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not guarantee they will yield to you.
questions.explanation: Never assume eye contact means a driver will yield to you. Drivers often look directly at motorcycles but do not see them.

questions.question: What should you do to maintain control while turning?

options.text: Increase your speed before entering the turn.
Look through the turn to see what is ahead.
Come to a complete stop before entering the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look through the turn to see what is ahead.
questions.explanation: To stay in control through a turn, look through the turn by turning only your head. Slow down before turning and lean your motorcycle in the right direction.

questions.question: If hazards are on your left, you should ride:

options.text: In the left portion of the lane.
In the right portion of the lane.
In any portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the right portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: When hazards are on your left, ride in the right portion of the lane. Adjust your position as road and traffic conditions change.

questions.question: A helmet will NOT provide the best protection if:

options.text: It is certified by the DOT.

questions.correctAnswerText: It has cracks.
questions.explanation: A good helmet must meet DOT standards, fit snugly, and have no defects. Cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps reduce protection.

questions.question: If you shift to a lower gear while going too fast, what happens?

options.text: The motorcycle lurches and the rear tire may skid.
The front tire will likely skid.
The engine makes a loud noise.

questions.correctAnswerText: The motorcycle lurches and the rear tire may skid.
questions.explanation: Shifting to a lower gear while going too fast causes the motorcycle to lurch suddenly and the rear wheel may skid.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should:

options.text: Be flexible about your lane position and adjust to changing conditions.
Travel faster than usual to reach your destination more quickly.
Always use your low beam headlight to see better.
Stay very close to the vehicle ahead of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be flexible about your lane position and adjust to changing conditions.
questions.explanation: At night, be flexible with your lane position and adjust to changing conditions. Use safe riding strategies in poor visibility.

questions.question: If you are riding next to another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Stay alongside until the next exit.
Let the other driver handle it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up or slow down.
questions.explanation: Riding directly next to another vehicle is unsafe. You may be in their blind spot, and they could block your escape route. Speed up or drop back instead.

questions.question: Which sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.
